themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

lesson.title: Causation in Global Conflict
lesson.summary: How the world wars, the Depression, and the interwar crises were connected.
learningGoals: Explain the relative significance of the causes of global conflict in the period 1900 to the present.
lesson.bigIdea: The two world wars were connected through the unresolved settlement of 1919 and the crises of the 1930s, and together they reshaped global power.
lesson.context: Causation is an AP reasoning process. Strong answers trace chains of cause and effect.

sections.title: A chain of conflict

blocks.text: World War I destroyed four empires and produced a resented peace. The Great Depression weakened democracies and strengthened extremists. Fascist and Japanese expansion then led to World War II.
World War II weakened European empires and left the United States and Soviet Union as superpowers, setting the stage for the Cold War and decolonization.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Each crisis created conditions for the next: war led to a flawed peace, the Depression to extremism, and extremism to a second war.

sections.takeaway: Global conflicts from 1914 to 1945 formed a connected chain of causes.

connections.title: From world war to Cold War
connections.body: Unit 8 traces how the superpowers' rivalry and the decline of empires shaped the world after 1945.
connections.transferQuestion: How did World War II set the stage for the Cold War?
connections.feedback: Explain the shift in global power.
